title: A swaying wall of singing on the Anfield terrace
episode: 1974: The KOPITES of Liverpool FC | The Kop | Classic BBC sport | BBC Archive
description: A 1974 BBC film on the Kop, the vast standing terrace behind one goal at Anfield, Liverpool FC’s stadium, named after Spion Kop, a Boer War hill. Its crowd swayed and sang as one. The terrace became all-seated in 1994.

title: Everton fans tell their own club’s story
episode: Everton FC: A history of the people's club told by the fans | Your Shout
description: Everton supporters tell the history of their club, founded by a Methodist chapel side in 1878. From 1892 Everton played at Goodison Park in Walton, one of the oldest purpose-built football grounds, before moving to Bramley-Moore Dock in 2025.

title: An electric railway on stilts along the docks
episode: Places - Lost in Time: The Liverpool Overhead Railway (Reworked)
description: Rail historian Ruairidh MacVeigh on the Liverpool Overhead Railway, an electric elevated line opened in 1893 above the Dock Road, past docks such as Stanley Dock. Known as the dockers’ umbrella, it closed in 1956 and was pulled down soon after.

title: A temple for concerts and courts opposite Lime Street
episode: Historian Steve Binns tells us the history St Georges Hall | The Guide Liverpool
description: Historian Steve Binns on St George’s Hall, the neoclassical concert hall and law courts of 1854 opposite Lime Street station. Its young architect, Harvey Lonsdale Elmes, died before it was finished; its floor of some 30,000 Minton tiles is usually covered.

title: Victorian painters who rejected the art academy
episode: An Introduction to the Pre-Raphaelites | National Museums Liverpool
description: National Museums Liverpool introduces the Pre-Raphaelites, the Victorian painters around Dante Gabriel Rossetti, John Everett Millais and William Holman Hunt. The Walker Art Gallery on William Brown Street has one of the major collections of their work.

title: The cathedral that would have outdomed St Peter’s
episode: Liverpool’s Unbuilt Cathedral That Could Have Rivalled St Peter’s
description: Architect Edwin Lutyens designed a Catholic cathedral for Liverpool with a dome larger than St Peter’s in Rome. Work began in 1933 and halted with the war; only the brick and granite crypt was built, and the 1967 cathedral now sits on top of it.
